strategy_name: Establish a statewide infrastructure of Community Collaboratives, state partners, lived experience experts, policymakers, and other stakeholders to address barriers related to prevention.
Identify legislative and/or administrative policy and practice improvements that impact prevention.
Community Collaboratives and local schools work together to offer extended learning opportunities and summer learning opportunities in communities across the state.
Community Collaboratives lead/participate in community efforts to expand high quality early childhood opportunities and home and center-based childcare.
Enrich the NE Early Learning Library with a special focus on family and community engagement.
Increase opportunities and access to multi-generational family literacy programming in communities and local schools
Develop new partnerships and innovative technology solutions that provide supported pathways for postsecondary education, career training, and adult education
Provide culturally and linguistically appropriate support to Afghan refugee students and families.
Develop "warmline" utilizing existing community-based prevention system infrastructure in Nebraska (Bring Up NE).
Community Collaboratives develop a sustainability plan/plan for capacity-building for long-term sustainability of community-based prevention.
Training and capacity-building of core competencies for Community Well-Being and community-based prevention.
Develop shared language, definition, and principles of "lived experience partnership".
Implement data-driven programs and activities that engage parents and lived experience partners for prevention in communities.
Develop interoperable platform (FindHelp) that will connect central navigation to other referral and data systems.
Identify indicators for well-being and thriving families.
Implement local councils or committees comprised of lived experience partners to co-create solutions.
Implement best practices for authentic partnership with lived experience experts that leads to co-creation of prevention strategies.
Provide access to youth, parent, and caregiver skill-building trainings, leadership development, and educational activities in communities.
Complete local Landscape Assessments to identify recommendations for coordination of services to address the needs of children and families.
Communication (local and statewide) is accessible to all.
Develop and implement strategic communication pathways between Community Collaboratives and NE state partners.
Strengthen relationship between Local Education Agencies (LEA), Institutions for Higher Education (IHE), Community Collaboratives, and state partners.
Identify and access diverse funding streams to serve transition-aged youth and systems-involved youth and young adults
Develop and strengthen local youth and young adult councils, committees, and programming to improve social connections and socio-emotional well-being
Support existing and scale the infrastructure in Nebraska for systems involved older youth strategies and programming.
Address policies and regulations to reduce barriers for childcare staffing and capacity in communities.
Increase home visitation capacity statewide.
Increase availability of mental health services that are connected to schools.
Identify and access public funding sources to align, braid, and blend for a sustainable continuum of care for mental and behavioral health services.
Reduce barriers to increase access to basic needs in communities for youth and families.
Utilize data to determine availability and accessibility of concrete supports for basic needs in communities.
Establish connections and partnerships with Community Support Specialists.
Identify underutilized funding streams for community-based prevention infrastrucutre, coaching, and to meet basic needs.
Qualify an increased number of Nebraska approaches for entry as evidence-based programs for sustainability.
Increase the availability of trauma sensitive and informed care training for providers and practitioners.
Develop a plan for employers of the well-being workforce in Nebraska to be trained in trauma-informed practices to support the workforce in their role in prevention.
Increase availability and opportunities for training on Protective and Promotive Factors.
Enhance existing training to offer culturally competent and culturally specific training on Protective and Promotive Factors.
Nebraska's well-being workforce has access to training, coaching, and mentoring for implementation of emerging practices and upward mobility in their own career pathways.
Nebraska's well-being workforce utilizes technology to address geographical and language barriers for training and capacity-building opportunities.
